title: Anderon Extends IBM's Semiconductor Legacy To Quantum Foundry Services
key_facts: The US Department of Commerce finalised a CHIPS and Science Act R&D award of up to $1 billion for Anderon, a quantum foundry IBM established this year; announced 16 Sep 2026.
IBM is matching it with $1 billion in cash plus intellectual property, assets and staff.
Anderon is based in Albany, New York, on the Albany NanoTech site where IBM has made quantum wafers for over five years; its first wafers are on a 300-millimetre line.

It aims to do for quantum chips what TSMC did for conventional chips, letting designers build chips without their own factory; CEO Mukesh Khare hopes to deliver wafers to outside customers by end of 2026.
Rigetti Computing is in talks with Anderon, according to its CEO Subodh Kulkarni, who says the test is yield as specifications tighten.
Anderon advertises superconducting qubit arrays; other qubit types would need extra process development not yet detailed.
quote_evidence: The U.S. Department of Commerce has finalized a CHIPS and Science Act R&D award of up to $1 billion for Anderon, a quantum foundry IBM established earlier this year.
If Anderon is successful, it could do for quantum hardware what TSMC did for conventional chips.
Time will tell which model will prevail. Perhaps both will co-exist, he says.
why_it_matters_hint: A shared factory for quantum chips could cut the cost for other makers, but it still needs customers beyond IBM.
event_date: 16 Sep 2026 (award announcement); IEEE Spectrum article 7 Oct 2026
notes: Forbes (Tirias Research) article of 9 Oct was blocked (403) and not read, so the entry uses IEEE Spectrum's report of the same subject. Underlying award is from 16 Sep 2026, so stale and scored one point lower. Whether the Forbes piece adds a new development is unknown.
